chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Jamil ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said:
I heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام say:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله would fast so much that it was said, he does not break the fast, and he would break the fast so much that it was said, he does not fast. Then he fasted one day and broke the fast one day. Then he fasted on Monday and Thursday. Then he came from that to fasting three days in the month: Thursday at the beginning of the month, Wednesday in the middle of the month, and Thursday at the end of the month. And he صلى الله عليه وآله used to say: 'That is the fasting of the lifetime.'

And my father عليه السلام used to say: 'There is no one more detested to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than a man to whom it is said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to do such and such, and he says: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will not punish me for striving in salat (prayer) and sawm (fasting) — as though he sees that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله left something of merit out of inability to do it.'

key_terms.صَوْمُ ٱلدَّهْرِ: the fasting of a lifetime; meaning a pattern whose reward is like perpetual fasting
key_terms.صِيَامِ: fasting; the devotional act being described
key_terms.يَصُومُ: he fasts; refers to voluntary sawm (fasting) practice
key_terms.يُفْطِرُ: he breaks the fast; indicates days without fasting
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer); mentioned alongside fasting in devotional striving
key_terms.ٱلْإِثْنَيْنِ: Monday; one of the days on which he fasted
key_terms.ٱلْخَمِيسِ: Thursday; one of the recurring recommended fasting days
key_terms.ٱلْفَضْلِ: merit or extra virtue; what some wrongly imagine the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله left undone

ai.seo_question: What fasting practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله is recommended, and why should a believer not go beyond his sunnah (prophetic tradition)?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the varying patterns of the Messenger of Allah’s صلى الله عليه وآله voluntary fasting until it settled on fasting three days each month. It also teaches that true merit lies in following the Prophetic sunnah (prophetic tradition), and that presuming one can surpass the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله in devotional practice is blameworthy.
